Investing.com -- ServiceNow Inc (NOW) trades at $92.19, up 5.23% on Nov 23 as of 3:48 PM EST. It is down about 43% over 1 month and 46% over 1 year, and it sits near the $81.24 52-week low (market cap about $95B). The damage came from one event. After the Oct 28 Q3 report, the stock posted its worst single-day drop on record, about 27–31% depending on the source. The headline numbers were fine: revenue was $4.11B, up 20.5%. The trigger was a Q4 cRPO guide of 18.5% against roughly 19.5–19.8% expected, plus a first EPS miss in six quarters ($1.00 vs $1.02). cRPO is contracted revenue not yet recognized, so it is a read on future growth.

Broken, Not Bankrupt
Sentiment: Cracked Consensus

Analysts: Most kept buy-equivalent ratings but trimmed targets. Piper Sandler held $175, StoneX cut to $150, and BofA's downgrade call was on Fortinet, not ServiceNow. The consensus is "Moderate Buy". The October targets of $150–176 predate the crash and are stale.

Estimate revisions: EPS estimates are down about 8.4% over 30 days, and revenue estimates are flat. Margins are being questioned, not demand.

Sector and macro: Software has been hit by fears of AI disruption, and the stock has also been pressured by AI-chip export curbs and a hot CPI print.

Positioning: Options traders are moderately bearish, with the put/call ratio above its typical level. A Form 144 insider-sale filing and trimmed institutional stakes add to the pressure.

Fundamentals Still Hum

Growth: Revenue went from $5.90B (2021) to $13.28B (2025). Consensus sees $16.23B for FY2026 and $19.24B for FY2027 (FinQL as of Nov 23, 2026).

Cash: Levered FCF rose from $1.80B to $4.58B, a gross margin near 77.5% sits alongside it, and management has been buying back shares.

Valuation: P/E is 65.9x trailing (as of Sep 30, 2026) but only 22.3x forward. The FinQL fair value is $134.13, or 45.6% upside, and the analyst target upside is 68.9%. Fair-value models are estimates and can lag a regime change.

Bear points: Margins compressed, short-term obligations exceed liquid assets, and the price-to-book multiple is still high.

Today's big story: Reported SEC Probe: Could Nvidia Stock Fall To $92?

Update, Nov 23: Goldman rose about 4% in Monday morning trading, after Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and Nvidia jumped more than 30%. The S&P 500 fund (SPY) rose about 5%. This article explains Friday's fall, and its figures are at Friday's close.

Goldman Sachs (GS) stock fell 6.7% on Friday, November 20, 2026, while the S&P 500 fell 3.7%. Its peers fell too, Morgan Stanley among them with a 5.3% drop. On the same day, Goldman and Apollo priced a $44 billion bond sale to fund NVIDIA chips for SpaceX. So what was that deal, and what ties Goldman's business to AI spending?

Goldman Sachs dropped 6.7% in one session, far more than the market. If much of your savings is in Goldman shares, you may wonder how deep the drop could go and what you would keep if you sold. In a free 30-minute review, our partner advisory firm can show you ways to limit your loss if the stock falls further and to sell with a smaller tax bill. Book the free review.

What Ties Goldman's Business To AI Spending?

Goldman Sachs helps raise the money behind the AI build-out. On November 20, it and Apollo priced the notes to pay for NVIDIA Vera Rubin chips and related equipment for SpaceX. Investors wanted so many of the notes that the companies made the deal bigger. The two companies called it the largest GPU financing executed to date.

That work is part of a theme management stressed on the October 13 call, which covered Goldman's third quarter of fiscal 2026. Management said demand for computing power far exceeds supply, which creates openings to help develop financing structures for the shortfall. By the bank's own account, then, AI spending brings it more financing work.

That tie puts Goldman among AI-linked stocks, and Friday was a hard day for them. A sell-off in technology shares deepened the day after Anthropic's market debut, and Anthropic's own shares dropped.

Did Other Investment Banks Fall Too?

Yes, all the larger ones did. In its sub-industry, investment banking and brokerage, all 13 other companies worth $2 billion or more fell. Their median drop was 4.0%, and four of them fell 5% or more.

The wider financial sector fell less, with the XLF sector fund down 1.8%. All five of Goldman's peers fell, but none as far as Goldman. They are Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Citigroup and BlackRock. So the stock moved with its group, and its drop was larger than the group's median.

title: Bank of America Doubles EMEA Banking Team: Can Deal Revenues Grow?

Bank of America Doubles EMEA Banking Team: Can Deal Revenues Grow?

JPM
C
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Bank of America BAC is expanding its corporate banking presence across Europe, the Middle East and Africa ("EMEA") to strengthen dealmaking opportunities. The bank has doubled its regional corporate banking team to approximately 150 bankers. BAC targets 40% growth in its EMEA corporate client base over the medium term, aiming to deepen relationships and capture additional investment-banking ("IB") business.

The expansion could support deal revenues by increasing BAC's access to corporate financing, mergers and acquisitions (M&A), and capital-market transactions. A broader client network should create opportunities to secure more advisory and underwriting mandates while cross-selling treasury, lending and payment services. The bank aims to increase the IB share among corporate clients from 9.3% to 12-14%, potentially strengthening its competitive position.

BAC's historical performance demonstrates its deal-revenue potential. Corporation-wide IB fees increased 7% year over year to $6.63 billion in 2025, supported by higher advisory and debt issuance fees. In the first nine months of 2026, fees rose 16% to $5.78 billion, driven by stronger advisory, equity and debt issuance activity. Global Banking IB fees increased to $3.14 billion from $2.71 billion.

However, third-quarter 2026 corporation-wide IB fees declined 11% year over year to $1.80 billion, reflecting weaker advisory and debt issuance activity. This highlights the sensitivity of deal revenues to transaction volumes and market conditions.

Expanding corporate coverage could help BAC capture more mandates, although actual fee realization will depend on deal completions and financing demand.

How Are BAC's Peers Positioned in Investment Banking?

JPMorgan Chase JPM continues to benefit from its extensive corporate banking relationships and global IB franchise. In the first nine months of 2026, JPMorgan's IB fees increased 24% year over year to $9.17 billion. Third-quarter fees rose 14% to $3.01 billion, supported by stronger advisory activity.

JPMorgan's established corporate network and cross-selling capabilities position it to capture additional M&A and underwriting opportunities, intensifying competition for BAC's expanding EMEA business.

Citigroup Inc. C is another major competitor, leveraging its international corporate banking network to generate financing and advisory mandates. Citigroup's integrated banking platform combines treasury and trade solutions, lending, debt underwriting and M&A advisory services. Stronger relationships with multinational corporations could support IB fee growth, although competition from BAC and JPM may challenge Citigroup's ability to capture additional market share.

Key Takeaways

Bank of America cut its MercadoLibre price target to $2,000 from $2,400 on Nov. 19 and kept its Buy rating, 48% above the Nov. 20 close.

MercadoLibre is giving up margin to stay ahead of rivals, including Sea Limited's Shopee in Brazil and Nu Holdings in credit.

On 2028 earnings estimates, $2,000 is 27x, below any forward multiple the stock has traded at in five years.

The valuation looks fair, but estimates keep falling, so $2,000 will likely take more than 12 months to reach.

MercadoLibre (MELI:NASDAQ) stock has lost 29% in a year, closing at $1,355.00 on Nov. 20. On Nov. 19, Bank of America cut its price target to $2,000 from $2,400 and kept its Buy rating, 48% above that close. The bank also lowered its 2026 to 2028 EPS estimates, saying the company is putting off monetization to reinvest in its lead.

MercadoLibre is spending heavily against two well-funded rivals: Sea Limited (SE:NYSE)'s Shopee in Brazil, and Nu Holdings (NU:NYSE) in credit.

A margin MercadoLibre chose to give up

Sea can afford the fight. Shopee's adjusted EBITDA rose 44.7% to $269.2 million in the third quarter, its most profitable quarter ever. Sea CEO Forrest Li said Brazil remained Shopee's fastest-growing market, and its new instant delivery service there already delivers in under four hours from more than 7,000 partner stores.

MercadoLibre's Nov. 4 report showed the cost of keeping up. Revenue rose 45% to $10.75 billion, but GAAP operating income fell 6.6% to $676 million. That's a 6.3% margin, against 9.8% a year earlier. Management tied the drop to more free shipping, nearly 20% more fulfillment space added from the prior quarter ahead of peak season, and heavier affiliate marketing in Brazil.

Bank of America is betting on the card

Analyst Robert Ford Aguilar has made Mercado Pago's credit card a big part of his case. In a June note, he forecast a $443 million EBIT loss on the card in 2026, breakeven in 2028 and $1.5 billion of EBIT by 2030. He put MercadoLibre's share of Brazil's card balances at 3.4% in March. Nu's credit portfolio rose 33% in a year, FX-neutral, while MercadoLibre's rose 62%, to almost $18 billion.

Investors may be wondering what's going on with Bank of America (NYSE:BAC)stock, as it has trailed other large bank stocks in recent weeks.

The second-largest bank in the U.S. has seen its share price plummet by about 5% during the past month (as of Nov. 19) to $48.57 per share. And since it hit a 52-week high of $65.23 on Aug. 17, it has dropped about 25%.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Meanwhile, the KBW Nasdaq Bank Index, which tracks the 24 largest U.S. banks, has fallen about 3% during the past month and 15% during the past three months..

So why has Bank of America stock lagged behind its major competitors, and is it a buy at recent prices?

Image source: Getty Images.

Bank of America underperformed in Q3

Bank of America did not have a great third quarter, missing revenue and earnings estimates.

Overall, revenue rose 3% to $30 billion but that missed Wall Street estimates of $30.7 billion. Net interest income (NII) accounted for more than half of that, up 8% to about $16.4 billion, on higher loan and deposit balances and a net yield that was 15 basis points higher at 2.16%.

But what hurt Bank of America more than other megabanks was its lackluster trading and investment banking results. Trading revenue fell by 5% when the company had expected it to be little changed. Investment banking was worse, with revenue down about 11% year over year in Q3.

By comparison, it underperformed the other big banks as JPMorgan Chase (NYSE:JPM), Citigroup (NYSE:C), and Wells Fargo (NYSE:WFC) all had double-digit percentage gains in investment banking fees. JPMorgan Chase and Citigroup also had solid gains in trading, while Wells Fargo was down 1%, but better than Bank of America.

After the results were released in mid-October, Wells Fargo analyst Mike Mayo called Bank of America's capital markets performance "easily worst in class."

In investment banking, Bank of America missed out on some hotter parts of the market, including debt underwriting and artificial intelligence (AI) financing. And equity underwriting grew only 3.4%, lagging behind its rivals. In trading, Bank of America saw fixed income trading decline 17% while global debt issuance was up 10% in Q3.

Big fine hurts earnings

Earnings also fell short of estimates, with Bank of America reporting earnings of $0.91 per share. However, that was offset by a $0.17-per-share hit from a $1.2 billion Treasury Department fine for violations of anti-money-laundering rule compliance. Without this fine, EPS was $1.08 per share, which was still below the average estimate of $1.10 per share.
